summary: Shows generating the WinRM client certificate with PowerShell New-SelfSignedCertificate, exporting cert.pem and cert.pfx, cleaning up the store, and converting the pfx to a PEM private key with OpenSSL. Only the control node needs the private key.
questions: How do I create a WinRM auth certificate with PowerShell?
How do I convert a PFX to a PEM private key for Ansible?
Does the Windows host need the private key for certificate auth?

answer_card.title: Generating the client certificate with PowerShell
answer_card.answer_md:
Create it with `New-SelfSignedCertificate` using `TextExtension = @("2.5.29.37={text}1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2","2.5.29.17={text}upn=$username@localhost")`, export `cert.pem` and `cert.pfx`, then remove the cert and key from the store.

PowerShell can't produce a PKCS8 PEM key, so convert with OpenSSL:

```bash
openssl pkcs12 -in cert.pfx -nocerts -nodes -passin pass: |
  sed -ne '/-BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-/,/-END PRIVATE KEY-/p' > cert.key
```

`cert.pem` and `cert.key` stay on the control node; the Windows host doesn't need the private key.
